# Claude Code Desktop + Remote Control + Claude Code on the web + Cowork/Dispatch — UX flows, interaction and visual design

Research date: 2026-09-03. Lens: user journeys, information architecture, attention management, keyboard affordances, visual language. Evidence is labeled **OBSERVED** (seen in official docs text, docs screenshots, or changelog entries) or **INFERRED** (my reading of mechanisms / reviewer reports). Docs pages were read as raw markdown (`<slug>.md`) from code.claude.com; the two seed slugs `get-started-desktop` and `dynamic-workflows` 404 today — the live pages are `desktop-quickstart` and `workflows`.

## 0. The surface map (what runs where, what the client is)

| Surface | Code runs on | Client UI | What is unique to it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop app, Code tab (Local / SSH / WSL session) | Owner's machine | Electron-style app: sidebar + arrangeable panes | Automatic per-session git worktrees, diff comments + "Review code", CI status bar with auto-fix/auto-merge, terminal/file/browser/iOS-sim panes, side chat, cross-session messaging, task chips, computer use, local scheduled tasks |
| Desktop app, Cloud session | Anthropic VM (or self-hosted runner) | Same app; some panes disabled | Survives app close; multi-repo; no terminal/file pane/`@mention`/plugins UI |
| claude.ai/code (web) | Anthropic VM | Browser | Onboarding via GitHub App; share sessions; Routines page; diff + inline comments; teleport to terminal |
| Remote Control | Owner's machine (CLI, VS Code, or Desktop-hosted) | claude.ai/code or Claude mobile app | Window into a local session: full local env, queued messages/permissions during reconnect, push notifications, Devices card to start sessions on a machine from the phone |
| Mobile Code tab | Cloud VM or (via RC) owner's machine | Claude iOS/Android app | Thin client only; photos/files attach; deep links `claude://code/...` |
| Cowork → Dispatch | Owner's machine (Desktop app) | Persistent single thread in Cowork tab, mirrored on phone | Router that decides "this is dev work" and spawns a Code session tagged **Dispatch**; outcome-oriented messaging; push on done / needs approval |

Sources: desktop.md, remote-control.md, claude-code-on-the-web.md, mobile.md, platforms.md, support article 13947068 (all read 2026-09-03).

## 1. Information architecture

### 1.1 Desktop Code tab (OBSERVED unless noted)
- **Three tabs**: Chat / Cowork / Code. Since the April 14 2026 redesign the switcher is three icons in the sidebar rather than word marks (TheNewStack, 2026-04-14). Code tab entry is "top center" per quickstart; VentureBeat (2026-04-15) found it by hovering the top-left icon — i.e. discoverability of the Code surface itself was a reported hurdle.
- **Sidebar = session list.** Every session has its own chat history, project folder, and code changes. Controls at the top filter by **status, project, environment** and group by project. Hover → archive icon. Sessions spawned by Dispatch carry a **Dispatch** badge; scheduled-task runs land under a **Scheduled** section; a **Routines** page (local + cloud) and a **Customize** page (connectors/skills/plugins) hang off the sidebar / "More" menu. Session title is renamed by clicking it in the toolbar.
- **Prompt area is the launcher.** Before the first message you set four things in the prompt box itself: Environment (Local / Cloud / SSH / WSL, gear icon on Local opens an encrypted env-var editor), Project folder, Model (dropdown next to send), Permission mode (selector next to send; remembered per folder, Plan is session-only). No separate "new session" wizard.
- **Panes**: chat, diff, browser, terminal, file, plan, tasks, subagent, iOS Simulator (macOS). Drag by header, resize by edge, `Cmd+\` closes the focused pane, Views menu opens more. **Two sessions side-by-side** by Cmd-clicking a second sidebar session; clicking a third replaces whichever pane has focus.
- **Session toolbar**: title, server dropdown (start/stop dev servers, "Persist sessions" for cookies), Views menu, a VS Code icon that opens the **Continue in** menu (→ Web or → IDE), and a **usage ring** next to the model picker (context usage per session + plan usage shared across surfaces; hover/click only — VentureBeat criticized that it is not always-on).
- **Transcript density is a first-class control**: Transcript view dropdown / `Ctrl+O` cycles **Normal** (tool calls collapsed to summaries) / **Verbose** / **Summary** (only final responses + changes) — the docs explicitly recommend Summary "when you're running multiple sessions and want to scan results quickly".
- **Docs screenshot (iOS Simulator page, 2048×1152)**: dark UI; header has a laptop glyph + session title "Acme Field" and four small mono-tone toolbar icons (share, terminal, diff/file, run). Transcript: user bubbles right-aligned in a soft grey card; assistant text plain; collapsed tool rows as single dim lines with a `›` chevron ("Edited 3 files ›", "Built AcmeField ›", "Background shell completed xcodebuild -scheme Soyary"); turn footer is an **orange asterisk + "41s · 2.9k tokens"**. Bottom bar: branch chip `main`, diff stat pill `+184 −37` (green/red numerals), `Create PR ▾`; composer placeholder "Describe a task or ask a question"; below it an amber **"Auto mode"** chip, `+`, mic, and `Opus` with a small blue ring on the right. The simulator pane has its own header with device/FPS/resolution/encoding pickers and a pill "● Claude is using this device" overlaid on the phone screen.

### 1.2 claude.ai/code (web) and the mobile Code tab
- Web: sidebar of sessions; hover → archive; archived filter reveals delete; session title dropdown → rename/archive/delete; visibility toggle Private/Public (Pro/Max) or Private/Team; a **Routines** page at claude.ai/code/routines. Each session shows a `+42 -18` indicator that opens the diff view. A **CI status bar** appears once a PR exists, holding the **Auto-fix** toggle. Environment-expired sessions are marked as such in the list.
- Mobile (docs screenshot, 1206×895, Week 34): near-black background, page title "Code", a **Devices** card at the top listing the machine running `claude remote-control` (`Lydias-MacBook-P…` with a laptop glyph and a **green dot**), a `+` to add, then **Sessions** with an `All ▾` filter; each row = dashed spinner tile, name `lydias-macbook-pro-local-buzzing-p…`, subtitle **"Connected"** in green with a laptop glyph, age `5d` at right. Everything is large-type, one state word per row, no tool text.
- Remote Control sessions "show a computer icon with a green status dot when online"; a session goes **offline within seconds** of the CLI exiting (changelog 2.1.236).

### 1.3 Agent view (CLI `claude agents`) — the reference model for "watch N agents"
Docs screenshot (1772×780): terminal, header "Claude Code v2.1.140 · Opus 4.7 (1M context) · /Users/jane/code/web-app · **1 awaiting input · 1 working · 2 completed**", then groups **Needs input** (row highlighted, yellow `✻`, question text "Should the API client retry on 429, or surface the error to the caller?", `12m`), **Working** (animated `✽`, "Editing src/components/Settings.tsx", `3m`), **Completed** (green `•`, "github.com/acme/web-app/pull/142", `40m`). Footer: "enter to open · space to reply · ctrl+x to delete · ? for shortcuts". Additional OBSERVED rules: groups **Pinned / Ready for review / Needs input / Working / Completed**; `Ready for review` = has an open PR; PR label `#1234` colored yellow (waiting/failed checks) / green (checks pass) / purple (merged) / grey (draft/closed); row summaries are written by a Haiku-class model (refreshed ≤ every 15 s from output, rewritten at turn end and every few minutes); **peek** (`Space`) shows the exact question with numbered choices and a `waiting 3m` staleness clock; `Tab` fills a suggested reply; completed rows fold into `… N more` while failures and open PRs stay visible; terminal tab title reads `2 awaiting input · claude agents`; inside a normal session the footer shows `← 2 agents` (count of agents waiting on you). This is the same vocabulary the Desktop sidebar filters by status, and VGV's review confirms Desktop shows "running / needs your attention / finished and created a PR" per session.

## 2. Journeys

### 2.1 First run — what must happen before the first useful result
**Desktop, Local** (OBSERVED): install → sign in → click Code → choose Local → Select folder → (model, mode preselected) → type task → Enter. On Windows Git must be installed first. In Manual mode the first result is a diff with Accept/Reject; in Auto/Accept-edits a `+12 -1` indicator appears. Gotcha: the app does not inherit your full shell env (only PATH + a fixed set from `~/.zshrc`), so "session not finding installed tools" is a documented troubleshooting item.
**Web** (OBSERVED): claude.ai/code first screen pushes the desktop app ("Continue on web" is at the bottom) → Sign in with GitHub → optional Claude GitHub App install (needed only for Auto-fix; **Skip** is offered) → Default environment auto-created on Pro/Max (form on Team/Enterprise) → repo selector under the input, branch selector, mode dropdown → Enter. Alternative: `/web-setup` in the terminal syncs the `gh` token and opens the browser.
**Remote Control** (OBSERVED): needs claude.ai login (API key, gateway, Bedrock all disqualify), workspace trust already accepted, and — notably — none of `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`/`DO_NOT_TRACK`/`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` set, or the feature is silently unavailable. Then `claude remote-control` prints a URL; spacebar shows a QR; `/mobile` shows an app-download QR. Push requires two `/config` toggles on the CLI side after installing the app.
**Dispatch** (OBSERVED, support article): open Cowork → Dispatch → "Get started" → "I'm signed in on my phone" → toggle file access + keep-awake → Finish. Pro/Max only; limited beta.

Rating. *Excellent*: the prompt box doubles as the whole configuration surface (environment/folder/model/mode) so there is no wizard; web onboarding degrades gracefully (Skip the GitHub App, Default env auto-created). *Friction*: four independent onboardings (Desktop, Web/GitHub, RC, Dispatch) with different prerequisites; RC eligibility depends on invisible env vars and account entitlement caches (the troubleshooting section lists nine distinct failure strings); Desktop asks for a specific subfolder rather than a workspace, which VentureBeat found locks you into one project at a time. *Why*: each surface was born as a separate product (CLI, cloud, Cowork) and the "where does it run" decision is pushed onto the user at the top of every flow instead of being inferred.

### 2.2 The daily loop — start work, watch N agents, get pulled in only when needed, review, ship
- **Start**: `Cmd+N` new session; each gets its own worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` (branch prefix configurable); `Ctrl+Tab` cycles sessions; Cmd-click splits two sessions.
- **Delegate without leaving**: when Claude notices out-of-scope work it offers a **task chip** in the chat; clicking it starts a new session in its own worktree while the current one continues (OBSERVED). Claude can also list/read/message/rename/archive the other desktop sessions on request; messages arrive in the other session as a **card labeled with the sending session's title and a link back**, are **held until that session finishes its current work**, and archiving always asks first in every mode. In the CLI the same message shows as a dim one-line `› Message from @api-worker: … (ctrl+o to expand)` preview (2.1.247).
- **Watch**: sidebar status filters; Summary transcript mode; **tasks pane** for subagents/background shells/dynamic workflows (click → subagent pane or stop); workflows show an approval card (name, phase list, token caution, **Once / Always / Deny**) and progress in the Background tasks pane. Subagents run in the background by default since 2.1.198 and their permission prompts surface in the main session with the asking agent named (2.1.186).
- **Get pulled in**: OS notification when a session finishes and you are not viewing it; desktop notification when CI finishes; Dispatch push when done/needs approval; `Notification` hook `agent_needs_input` / `agent_completed` in agent view. A 2.1.247 change adds a one-keystroke **"Yes, and switch to auto mode"** to Bash permission prompts — the product is actively trying to make you stop being pulled in.
- **Steer without stopping**: type a correction and press Enter while Claude runs; it is read after the current action completes. `Esc` stops.
- **Side question**: `Cmd+;` / `/btw` opens a side chat that reads the whole main thread but writes nothing back; not persisted to disk; local/SSH/WSL only.
- **Limits**: usage-limit card offers "Auto-continue when limits reset" with the retry time (w33).

Rating. *Excellent*: the state vocabulary (Needs input / Working / Ready for review / Completed) is consistent across sidebar, agent view, mobile; task chips turn scope creep into parallelism with one click; held cross-session messages respect the receiving agent's turn; Summary mode is the right density for a many-agent glance. *Friction*: VGV reports side panels (plan/tasks) open per session and pile up, "you spend time managing windows"; git controls are almost entirely delegated to the agent; built-in buttons (Create PR) cannot be rebound to your own skill; the usage ring is hover-only. *Why*: the pane system optimizes for one deep session, while the sidebar optimizes for many shallow ones — the two layers were not designed as one attention model (INFERRED).

### 2.3 Away from the desk — the phone flow
- **What you can do** (OBSERVED, remote-control.md + mobile.md): read the transcript live; send messages (queued if mid-turn and kept in the transcript); attach photos (seen directly; also saved under `~/.claude/uploads/` with the path told to Claude) and files (downloaded to the machine and passed as `@` refs); answer permission prompts and `AskUserQuestion`s (these stay open indefinitely); see and **Stop** subagents and workflows already running (per-task Stop fixed for CLI-hosted sessions in 2.1.238); open a **diff pane** of uncommitted changes (computed on the machine; falls back to branch-vs-default when clean); change **model** and **effort** from the device (applies to the local session, shown back in the terminal); see the session's current permission mode (published since 2.1.234); text-form commands only (`/model sonnet`, `/effort high`, `/compact`, `/clear`, `/config key=value`, `/mcp reconnect`). Since Week 34, a machine running `claude remote-control` appears as a **device card**; tapping it lets you pick a directory and start a brand-new session on that machine from the phone (`--spawn worktree` gives each such session its own worktree).
- **How you know something needs you**: push notifications when RC is on. Two toggles: **Push when Claude decides** (long task finished, or a decision needed) and **Push when actions required** (permission prompts and questions); you can also ask in the prompt ("notify me when the tests finish"). No per-event configuration beyond that. Dispatch has its own push (done / needs your go-ahead). Cowork cloud sessions notify the phone when finished or waiting.
- **Presence-aware suppression** (OBSERVED): pushes are skipped while you are typing in / focused on the connected terminal; `CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE` extends that to "any time you are at the machine" via a screen-lock marker file. In the other direction, the terminal shows **"Still working — Check in from your phone"** on long turns and **"Approve tool calls from your phone"** after several prompts — a handful of times total, not configurable.
- **Deliberately not on mobile**: Bypass permissions cannot be selected from the app in any session; Auto cannot be selected for a Remote Control session (RC from the app offers Manual / Accept edits / Plan); picker-style commands (`/plugin`, `/resume`, `/permissions`) are local-only; the terminal-only Fable usage-credits consent prompt is never forwarded; other forwarded dialogs auto-close after 5 minutes (`dialogExpiry`) and continue with the no-action default; side chats are not on mobile; plugins/connectors UI is absent in cloud sessions.
- **Recovery semantics on the phone**: "if your laptop sleeps or your network drops, Claude Code reconnects automatically… queues messages, permission prompts, and status updates … and delivers them once the connection recovers."

Rating. *Excellent*: the phone is a peer, not a viewer — model/effort/mode/stop/diff/attachments all round-trip; the presence rule ("don't buzz me while I'm typing here") is exactly the right default; the terminal nudges you toward the phone at the two moments it matters (long turn, prompt fatigue). *Friction*: the feature's own history is a list of "permission prompt never showed on the connected device" bugs (GitHub #52084 Apr 2026 closed as duplicate of #45942; changelog fixes in 2.1.202, 2.1.217, 2.1.238, 2.1.248, 2.1.252, 2.1.258) — the queued-delivery promise was repeatedly the thing that broke; the local process must stay alive, which pushes people to tmux; one remote session per interactive process. *Why*: correctness of "you will always see the pending ask" is a distributed-state problem (host TUI, relay, N clients, reconnects) and the UI has no visible "last known state / awaiting delivery" affordance to make partial failure honest (INFERRED).

### 2.4 The review moment — diff, comments, CI, PR
- **Diff**: `+12 -1` indicator → diff viewer with file list left, changes right (unified only; TheNewStack notes Codex offers split). Click any line → comment box → Enter; **Cmd+Enter submits all comments as one batch**; Claude applies them and produces a new diff. On the web the comments **queue until your next message and are bundled with it**, addressed as `at src/auth.ts:47, …`.
- **Review code** button (top-right of diff toolbar): Claude reviews the current diff and leaves comments inline in the same viewer, limited to compile errors, definite logic errors, security issues, obvious bugs (not style, not linter-class issues); you can reply to a comment or ask for revision.
- **PR**: `Create PR ▾` at the top of the diff/bottom bar (full / draft / GitHub compose page with generated title+body). After the PR exists a **CI status bar** appears: polls via `gh`, surfaces failures, **Auto-fix** (read failure output, iterate) and **Auto-merge** (squash; requires repo auto-merge enabled) toggles, desktop notification when CI finishes, optional **auto-archive** of the session on merge/close. On the web Auto-fix additionally subscribes to GitHub webhooks: clear fixes are pushed, ambiguous review comments are asked back, duplicates noted; Claude's replies on GitHub are posted under your account but labeled as Claude Code. Merge conflicts are explicitly not handled (no webhook).
- **In agent view** the PR number is the result: "review and merge the pull request when its number turns green".

Rating. *Excellent*: comments are batched into one instruction, which matches how people actually review (read everything, then send); "Review code" reuses the same comment surface instead of a separate report; the PR lifecycle (create → CI → fix → merge → archive) is a single status bar. *Friction*: no image rendering or file preview from the diff (VGV); no split view; git is agent-only. *Why*: the diff is treated as a conversation input, not as a git workspace — good for review, bad for the last-mile manual polish (INFERRED).

### 2.5 Recovery — network drop, machine sleep, crashed agent
- **RC network drop** (OBSERVED): interactive session keeps retrying for the outage's duration and reconnects (30-minute reconnect window since 2.1.232, HTTP-403 blips tolerated 3 minutes with the refusing party named); server mode gives up after ~10 minutes and exits. A **persistent failure indicator** replaces the old 8-second toast (2.1.224), with the reason, and a footer `/rc failed` state; the reason text distinguishes "taken over by another device", "ended/archived elsewhere", "server can't find it" and drops the reconnect advice in those cases.
- **Machine sleep**: RC reconnects on wake; background sessions (agent view) are preserved across sleep and their supervisor reconnects; a session mid-response at sleep may come back unresponsive and is restarted from where it left off when opened.
- **Server stopped**: `claude remote-control` / `--continue` / `--session-id` bring sessions back for ~4 hours; a crashed session in server mode is revived by simply messaging it from the phone.
- **Cloud environment expired**: session marked expired in the list; reopening provisions a fresh VM with history restored, but running subagents/shell work is lost; container restarts mid-turn re-run the interrupted turn and report lost background work (2.1.216, 2.1.247).
- **Desktop**: usage-limit auto-continue; "Failed to load session" for missing folder/LFS; 403 → sign out/in. Desktop-hosted RC sessions reattach to the same claude.ai session on resume instead of creating a duplicate (2.1.232).

Rating. *Excellent*: failure states are worded by cause and the UI stops suggesting the wrong remedy; "message it to revive it" is the lowest-friction crash recovery imaginable. *Friction*: three different lifetimes (4 h server memory, 5 min dialog expiry, ~30 d desktop transcript cleanup fixed in 2.1.248) that the user has to learn; recovery affordances live in the CLI footer, not in the phone UI. *Why*: the phone is a window, and the window cannot restart the thing behind it (INFERRED; the Devices card is the first step toward changing that).

## 3. Attention management and state model (summary)
- **Vocabulary**: Working (animated) · Needs input (yellow) · Idle (dimmed) · Completed (green) · Failed (red) · Stopped (grey); plus process shape (`✻` alive, `∙` exited-but-resumable, `✢` sleeping loop). Groups: Pinned / Ready for review / Needs input / Working / Completed. Mobile reduces this to one word ("Connected") plus a green dot; Desktop sidebar exposes it as filters. (OBSERVED)
- **Needs-attention queue exists everywhere**: agent view top group + counts in header and tab title; `← 2 agents` footer hint in a normal session; Desktop OS notification only when not viewing that session; push only when not present at the terminal. A session waiting on a sandbox / MCP-input / managed-settings prompt is classified as Needs input, not Working (2.1.212); a background session waiting to approve a cross-session message now says so and names the sender (2.1.257).
- **Interruptions are held, not dropped**: cross-session messages wait for the turn boundary; held messages open an approval dialog with sender + preview; `dialogExpiry` default 5 min except permission prompts and AskUserQuestion which never expire; while no terminal is attached the dialog stays open.
- **Titles**: auto-generated as short specific names ("Login button bug", 2.1.234), language-matched, appear after the first prompt (2.1.246), rename syncs CLI ↔ web/app both ways (2.1.221).

## 4. Keyboard / command affordances (OBSERVED)
Desktop: `Cmd+/` shortcut sheet; `Cmd+N` / `Cmd+W`; `Ctrl+Tab` / `Cmd+Shift+]` session cycling; `Esc` stop; `Cmd+Shift+D/B` diff/browser; `Cmd+Shift+S` select element in browser; `` Ctrl+` `` terminal; `Cmd+\` close pane; `Cmd+;` side chat; `Ctrl+O` view modes; `Cmd+Shift+M/I/E` permission-mode / model / effort menus; `1–9` picks in any open menu. No general command palette is documented; `/` in the prompt box browses built-in commands, skills and plugin skills, and `+` is the menu button. Agent view: arrows, `Space` peek, `Enter`/`→` attach, `←` background/detach, `Ctrl+S` regroup, `Ctrl+T` pin, `Ctrl+R` rename, `Ctrl+X` stop then delete, `Alt+1..9`, `?` help, `s:blocked` text filters.

## 5. Density and visual language (OBSERVED from the three docs screenshots, INFERRED where noted)
- **Dark by default in every screenshot**; the desktop transcript is low-contrast grey on near-black with tool activity collapsed to single dim lines. Color is reserved for state and numbers: green/red diff counts, amber "Auto mode" chip, orange asterisk turn marker, blue usage ring, green "Connected"/green dot. This is close to very-happy's "accent only for live" rule, except Anthropic uses *amber* for the risky mode and *orange* for "Claude is working/spent" rather than a single live color.
- **Type**: proportional sans everywhere in Desktop/mobile (mono only in the terminal pane and agent view); the mobile Code tab is large-type, one line of state per row.
- **Chrome is minimal**: a four-icon toolbar, no tabs bar, no status bar; the diff stat + Create PR live in a slim bar above the composer, i.e. the review entry point is always one click away from typing.
- **Agent view** is the densest surface: three columns (name / summary / age) and it still reads instantly because the group header carries the state.

## 6. What changed in the last ~3 months (June 1 → September 1, 2026; changelog 2.1.160–2.1.258 + weekly digests)
- Remote Control moved from research preview to GA (w34) with the **Devices card / start-on-machine-from-phone**; effort and model picks from the phone apply and echo back; permission mode published to clients (2.1.234); foreground subagent tool calls stream to the phone (2.1.251); RC footer pill (2.1.162) → persistent red `/rc failed` (2.1.178) → persistent failure indicator with reconnect shortcut (2.1.224); reattach to existing claude.ai session on resume (2.1.232); offline-within-seconds (2.1.236); per-task Stop from the phone (2.1.238); a long tail of "pending permission prompt not shown to connected device" fixes (2.1.202, 2.1.217, 2.1.238, 2.1.248, 2.1.252, 2.1.258).
- Desktop: in-app browser (w28), iOS Simulator pane (w30), auto-continue at usage limit (w33), `/design` artboards (w34), Dispatch-spawned sessions with 30-minute app approvals, workflow approval cards, desktop notification for asks queued under another dialog (2.1.257), desktop sessions no longer purged at 30 days (2.1.248).
- Multi-agent attention: cross-session messaging (2.1.224) → `@session` mention typeahead (2.1.232) → collapsed one-line message preview (2.1.247) → `notify_when_idle` (2.1.236); agent view rows became classifier-written headlines with a colored state word (2.1.205), peek leads with the question + `waiting 3m` (2.1.207), `/resume` picker in agent view (2.1.212), fork-to-background (2.1.212), subagents background by default (w27), auto mode default on Pro/Max/Team from Aug 14 (w32), "Yes, and switch to auto mode" on Bash prompts (2.1.247).
- Web: `/teleport` hint inside cloud sessions (2.1.223), `/web-setup` tip (2.1.243), auto-fix/ultrareview as background cloud sessions with task progress counts.

## 7. Take-aways for very-happy (short; the ranked list is in the structured output)
Borrow: the four-state vocabulary with a Needs-input group pinned to the top and counts in the tab title; classifier-written one-line row summaries; peek-and-reply without opening the transcript; batch diff comments sent as one instruction; task chips; presence-aware push with a screen-lock marker; explicit failure wording that tells you *not* to reconnect when you were taken over; a Devices card that lets the phone start a session on the Mac in a fresh worktree; "message the crashed session to revive it".
Avoid: per-session floating side panels that stack; hover-only usage; a single unbranched Dispatch thread; forwarding dialogs that silently expire; four separate onboardings keyed on "where it runs".
